method: Re-transcribed from tools/raw/20A-A-ex page images (printed exam); own derivations via brute force/networkx/sympy in tools/verify/20A-A/refute_r2_*.py, written before reading the claims.

ownAnswers.1c: m,n in {1,2} (m,n>=1); complement = K_m u K_n
ownAnswers.3c: complement of P_n (n vertices): connected for n=1 and n>=4; <=2 odd vertices iff n odd or n=4 -> n=4 or odd n>=5 (plus n=1 trivially; n=3 only if connectivity is dropped)
ownAnswers.5c: Petersen: complement 6-regular: Hamilton yes, Euler yes, bipartite no (triangle a,d,g), isomorphic no (15 vs 30 edges)
ownAnswers.6b: yes, both cardinality c; explicit bijection x->12-5x also exists

1c.note: m,n>=1 assumed, stated in the solution

2c.transcriptionIssue: printed Q2 has NO point values on any part; '(2 נק.)' and '(5 נק.)' (and 2a=10, 2b=8) come from the lecturer-solution version of the exam, not the printed sheet. Low severity: the 25 total is consistent.

3c.transcription: matches printed p2 (no n bound printed)
3c.convention: n>=2: not forced by the printed text. n=1 (single vertex) trivially has a length-0 Euler trail; and n=3 (one edge + isolated vertex) has a trail covering all edges if connectivity is not demanded. Fixer's reading (Euler trail needs a connected graph, P_1 excluded as edgeless) is the standard textbook one and gives n=4 or odd n>=5, but it is a choice, not the only reading. Suggest the solution say one line on n=1 and on n=3.
3c.firstDivergence: none in the answer set under the connected-graph definition

4b.convention: 'עולה' = non-decreasing is the natural reading: strict gives 0 (6 > 4 values), so no exam would ask it. The solution already says strict is impossible.

5a.note: assumes simple graph (loops/multi-edges not meant); Erdos-Gallai also fails. Consistent with the course.

5b.flag: step 2 prompt says 'במספרים טבעיים' for y1+..+y4=12 with y_i>=0. In this course N starts at 1 (the lecturer writes alpha,beta>=1, alpha,beta in N in 2c and 6a solutions), so that wording is wrong for y_i>=0; use 'שלמים אי-שליליים'. The answer is unaffected.
5b.transcription: matches printed p3 (22 letters, a>=3,b>=1,c>=4,d>=2, unordered)

5c.transcription: graph checked edge by edge against printed p3: it is the Petersen graph; printed points '2+3+3+3' read from the page crop
5c.convention: points 2+3+3+3 is the printed text (zoomed): natural.

6a.convention: n>=1: the printed text gives no range for n. n>=1 is the natural reading (N starts at 1 in this course, and n=0 gives phi(1)=1, where 2^(5n)3^(n-1)=1/3 fails). Solution notes the missing range. Fine.

6b.note: valid via Cantor-Bernstein; an explicit bijection (x->12-5x) is shorter and could be mentioned. Step 1 option b (explicit bijection) is described as not the method used, but it would also be a correct method; acceptable.
